children: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM, Financials) could be preparing to make more of its most advanced chips, and Wells Fargo says the opportunity may extend beyond TSMC itself.
The foundry is considering an increase in its 2-nanometer production plans, potentially creating additional demand for the equipment required to build leading-edge chips.

Wells Fargo said the expansion should be viewed as a potentially incremental opportunity for semiconductor equipment companies, although analysts cautioned that details including timing, size and production node still need confirmation.
The potential increase comes as demand for advanced manufacturing continues to rise across AI, smartphones and custom silicon.
TSMC sits at the center of that demand, manufacturing chips for companies including Apple, Nvidia, AMD and other major semiconductor designers.
Moving to smaller manufacturing nodes also requires increasingly sophisticated and expensive production equipment, meaning additional 2nm capacity can ripple through the semiconductor supply chain.

That makes TSMC's eventual production plans important beyond the foundry itself. Confirmation of the size and timing of any additional 2nm capacity could give investors a clearer picture of how much additional equipment spending may follow.

title: TSMC's 2nm Push Could Create a New Winner in the AI Chip Boom
